_about: Deep panels (research, per country). Figures for plants and projects come from atlas_world.json (GEM + LeadIT). certainty: high = official or primary source; medium = reported, estimated or disputed; low = interpretation.

overall.text: The single decision that shapes everything — the state agreement with Tata Steel — is not signed. Its deadline moved to 1 March 2027.

rows.v: CBAM's paying phase began 1 Jan 2026; free ETS allowances for steel are being phased out through 2034.
The EU is weighing an extension of free allowances beyond the agreed phase-out — which would weaken the economics of green steel.
Permanent EU safeguard since 1 Jul 2026: 50% duty above quota, quotas ~47% below 2024.

Formally still exists, but neutralised in Sept 2025: companies get an exempt amount most already stay under. Abolition planned, timing open (May 2026). Effective rate ~€21/t; €37–97M paid by all industry for 2025.
Letter of intent (2025) for a 'maatwerkafspraak'. Deadline moved from 30 Sept 2026 to 1 March 2027. Up to €2 bn from the state; needs European Commission approval.
Public Prosecution announced criminal prosecution of Tata Steel (July 2026). Province wants to revoke permits for the two coke plants.
Phase 1 (gas DRI + carbon capture) cuts ~40% CO₂ — below LeadIT's 85% 'green' threshold. It is a lower-carbon plant, not yet a green one.
Hydrogen at €5–8/kg vs €2.5–3/kg needed for viability (2024 figure). The full H₂ switch depends on closing this gap.

State says max €2 bn. Milieudefensie & SOMO estimate up to €10.8 bn including CCS, biomethane, grid and slag costs to 2045 (disputed by state and Tata). Court flagged risk of lasting subsidy dependence.
Stepwise and gas-first: build 'H2-ready' DRI, run it on gas with carbon capture, raise scrap from 17% to 30%, switch to hydrogen/biomethane later. Make the state co-own the risk.
May–June 2024: engineering contracts to Danieli & Tenova. 2025: letter of intent with the state. Sept 2026: CEO says engineering is nearly complete.

Zeremis Carbon Lite (since 2022): an allocated 'up to 90%' footprint reduction, verified by DNV — a book-keeping model, not physically green steel. Sold to processors Wuppermann, Bilstein, EMW, Arania.
Coastal site at IJmuiden on the North Sea — direct access for ore and coal ships.
Porthos (Rotterdam) stores 2.5 Mt CO₂/y from 2027 — enables the carbon-capture route.
Iron, steel and finishing (coated & automotive-grade coil) on one site.
North Sea wind as a future source of green power and hydrogen.
Expensive hydrogen and electricity compared with Nordic competitors (e.g. Stegra, HYBRIT in Sweden).
One plant carries the whole national transition — no portfolio to spread the risk.
Health complaints, prosecution, permit disputes, a growing slag stockpile.
Agreement deadlines keep moving; long-lead equipment orders wait for the deal.
Steel processors supplying automotive & industry (Zeremis deals). No named carmaker offtake found yet.
CBAM + safeguard make high-carbon imports dearer — a protected market, but not yet a premium for green.

overall.text: The furthest along in the world: every Swedish steel plant has a green project. But the flagship, Stegra, needed new money twice in 2026 as costs rose.

rows.v: CBAM's paying phase began 1 Jan 2026; free ETS allowances for steel are being phased out through 2034.
The EU is weighing an extension of free allowances beyond the agreed phase-out — which would weaken the economics of green steel.
Permanent EU safeguard since 1 Jul 2026: 50% duty above quota, quotas ~47% below 2024.
Fossil-free steel reportedly costs 15–25% more than conventional steel for Volvo.
Stegra says its costs are 'significantly higher than assumed' and seeks more capital (Oct 2026), months after a €1.4 bn round led by Wallenberg Investments (Apr 2026).
Strong if the plants start on time: cheap fossil-free power plus domestic ore. The risk is financial, not technical.
Go straight to hydrogen-DRI and electric furnaces, skipping gas as a bridge; secure premium buyers early.
SSAB: Oxelösund conversion decided in 2023; Luleå €4.5 bn EAF mini-mill (2.5 Mt/y), start-up targeted late 2028. Stegra Boden: 5 Mt/y of green steel, under construction.
HYBRIT's demonstration plant in Gällivare slipped to late 2027, with risk of 2028 (permitting).
Hydropower and wind in the north supply electricity and green hydrogen.
LKAB's iron ore and the HYBRIT alliance (SSAB, LKAB, Vattenfall) keep the value chain in one country.
A first-of-a-kind plant financed mostly privately: cost overruns hit hard.
Most output must be exported, so it depends on buyers abroad paying a premium.
Volvo Cars targets 100% renewable steel in models launched from 2030; Volvo Group the same for its trucks and machines.

overall.text: Europe's largest producer, with the most plans and the most mixed signals: one cancellation despite €1.3 bn of aid, Salzgitter delayed, thyssenkrupp building — but on gas first.

rows.v: CBAM's paying phase began 1 Jan 2026; free ETS allowances for steel are being phased out through 2034.
The EU is weighing an extension of free allowances beyond the agreed phase-out — which would weaken the economics of green steel.
Permanent EU safeguard since 1 Jul 2026: 50% duty above quota, quotas ~47% below 2024.
Subsidised industrial electricity price approved by Brussels (Apr 2026) for 2026–2028; floor of 5 ct/kWh; half the aid must go into decarbonisation.
High electricity prices and an uncertain energy mix were the reported reasons ArcelorMittal dropped its German plans.
thyssenkrupp's Duisburg DRI (~€3 bn) is about two-thirds publicly funded.
State-backed DRI conversions that start on natural gas; hydrogen postponed until it is cheaper.
thyssenkrupp: Brussels approved changed funding conditions so Duisburg can start without hydrogen (Aug 2026). Salzgitter: SALCOS phase 1 on track for 2027, phases 2–3 decision moved to 2028/29.
ArcelorMittal cancelled Bremen and Eisenhüttenstadt (Jun 2025), declining €1.3 bn of subsidies.
Large domestic buyers (automotive, machinery) close to the mills.
Federal and state funding already committed to several conversions.
Salzgitter blamed deteriorating economic and regulatory conditions since 2022 for its delay.
No affordable hydrogen yet; the first DRI plants will burn gas.
Lead markets and a green steel label are discussed but not yet binding on buyers.

overall.text: The incumbent's flagship — ArcelorMittal's hydrogen DRI in Gijón, backed by €450 M of public money — is suspended. A newcomer, Hydnum, is raising capital in Puertollano.

rows.v: CBAM's paying phase began 1 Jan 2026; free ETS allowances for steel are being phased out through 2034.
The EU is weighing an extension of free allowances beyond the agreed phase-out — which would weaken the economics of green steel.
Permanent EU safeguard since 1 Jul 2026: 50% duty above quota, quotas ~47% below 2024.
€450 M from Spain's recovery funds approved for the Gijón low-carbon project (2024).
ArcelorMittal cited deficiencies in CBAM, no domestic green hydrogen framework, and energy-market developments.
About 70% of Spanish steel capacity is already electric-arc, so the transition is mostly about the remaining blast furnaces.
Build the electric furnaces in Gijón and Sestao now; hold the DRI decision (2.3 Mt/y) until rules improve.
Hydnum Steel: hydrogen + renewable-powered steel in Puertollano; €150 M from the state co-investment fund (Aug 2026), >€1.5 bn package; construction to begin end 2026.
Strong solar and wind resources for cheap power and hydrogen.
The largest primary producer decides at group level, weighing Spain against other countries.
No large public offtake commitments found.

overall.text: ArcelorMittal confirmed a €1.3 bn electric furnace in Dunkirk (2 Mt/y, 2029) once CBAM and new tariffs were in place. GravitHy is permitting a 2 Mt/y hydrogen-iron plant in Fos.

rows.v: CBAM's paying phase began 1 Jan 2026; free ETS allowances for steel are being phased out through 2034.
The EU is weighing an extension of free allowances beyond the agreed phase-out — which would weaken the economics of green steel.
Permanent EU safeguard since 1 Jul 2026: 50% duty above quota, quotas ~47% below 2024.
Up to half of the Dunkirk furnace funded through energy-savings certificates; €850 M confirmed in 2023 for Dunkirk and Fos.
ArcelorMittal named CBAM's definitive phase and the new tariff quota as conditions that made Dunkirk possible.
Dunkirk alone emits about 15% of French industrial CO₂.
Electrify first with scrap-fed furnaces; leave hydrogen iron to specialised newcomers.
Dunkirk EAF confirmed 10 Feb 2026, start 2029. GravitHy filed building and environmental permits in Fos (Jul 2026).
Nuclear-heavy electricity makes electric furnaces low-carbon.
Decisions waited for EU trade protection: the Dunkirk confirmation took almost two years.
No large public offtake commitments found.

overall.text: Over half the world's steel, mostly from blast furnaces. A few large hydrogen-DRI demonstrations run, and the carbon market covers steel — with free allowances and a low price.

rows.v: 960.8 Mt of crude steel in 2025, down 4.4% — a seven-year low.
Record exports of over 119 Mt in 2025.
Steel joined the national ETS in 2025. Allowances are free and intensity-based; each firm's surplus or shortfall is capped at ±3%.
About CNY 94 per tonne (Sep 2026) — a fraction of the EU price.
Absolute caps for some sectors planned from around 2027; paid auctioning later.
With cheap, free carbon at home, the main pressure on emissions comes from abroad (CBAM on exports).
Baowu's Zhanjiang works runs a 1 Mt/y hydrogen-based shaft furnace since Dec 2023, using hydrogen-rich coke-oven gas.
Large state-led demonstrations and a soft carbon market first; tighten later as output falls.
Unmatched scale and supply chains, including electrolysers and renewables.
A large, relatively young blast-furnace fleet makes fast change expensive.
Falling domestic production and record exports point to weak demand at home.
